newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling edges up vs dollar, still rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling edges up vs dollar, still rangebound.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was marginally firmer on Wednesday boosted by modest inflows from the agricultural sector, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.44 versus the dollar from 53.46 on Tuesday, while against the pound, it was posted at a commercial mean of 87.39 from 87.46.
Some dealers said activity had picked up, recovering from the long weekend. Monday was a public holiday.
"Basically, what's happening now is all the dollars that were meant to be sold yesterday (Tuesday) and the day before are being sold now," one dealer said.
Dealers added that shilling fluctuations were marginal and that it appeared the currency would remain stuck at the 53.30/50 level.
"At the moment interest from the traditional big players -- oil and agriculture looks balanced," one dealer said, adding that the shilling was trading at 53.30/50 level at midday.
The money market was liquid. Overnight rates were unchanged at 10 percent.
